newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria's leader meets more politicians on poll.
newsitem.headline: Algeria's leader meets more politicians on poll.

text.p: Algerian President Liamine Zeroual on Thursday met 20 political leaders to discuss forthcoming parliamentary elections, officials and party sources said.
Officials and party sources said by telephone from Algiers that Zeroual discussed setting up an independent committee to supervise the elections, including security.
The talks were preceded on Tuesday by a five-hour meeting between Zeroual and 10 other party leaders to discuss preparations for the parliamentary elections planned for the first half of this year.

Political sources told Reuters by telephone that Zeroual, a former soldier, was striving to reassure politicians that his government would ensure security to protect voters and candidates in the poll.
Algeria has been without parliament since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which radical Islamists had taken a commanding lead.
According to the constitution adopted last November, the national assembly and the national council (upper house) form the parliament.

Two thirds of the national council's 144 members will be picked by the elected local authorities while the 48 others will be appointed by the president from the ranks of leading personalities, union officials and other professionals.
